source_refs.note: Book p. 177-178: 10.1.1 statement, proof with unit-circle figure, Note, Example 2. Example 2 uses sin(a+b), only deduced in 10.1.2 (v): a Teaching note says so. Teaching notes, Key points, Common mistakes are ours.

blocks.text: Pichle page par humne distance formula taaza kiya tha. Ab woh waqt aa gaya hai jis ke liye woh tayyar kiya tha: is unit ka sab se ahem qanoon. Yeh ek hi formula hai, lekin aage aane wale taqreeban saare formulas isi ke bachche hain. Is liye ise sirf ratta mat lagaiye; is ka saboot bhi samajhiye. Kitab kehti hai: maan lijiye \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) koi bhi do angles (real numbers) hain, to

blocks.text_alt: cos of (alpha minus beta) equals cos alpha cos beta plus sin alpha sin beta

blocks.text: Isi ko Fundamental Law of Trigonometry (trigonometry ka bunyadi qanoon) kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ise lafzon mein yaad kariye: do angles ke farq (difference) ka cos = (cos guna cos) jama (sin guna sin). Sign par khaas dhyan dein: bracket ke andar minus hai, lekin right side par plus aata hai. Yeh ulta sign hi is formula ki pehchaan hai.
Ise fundamental (bunyadi) kyun kehte hain? Kyun ke is unit ke baqi formulas, yani \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\), \(\sin(\alpha \pm \beta)\), \(\tan(\alpha \pm \beta)\), aur 10.2 ke allied angles wale saare results, isi ek qanoon se nikalte hain (agla page 10.1.2 dekhiye). Ek imaarat ki bunyaad samajh lein to poori imaarat samajh aa jati hai.

Ab saboot dekhte hain. Aasani ke liye kitab farz karti hai ke \(\alpha > \beta > 0\), yani dono angles positive hain aur \(\alpha\) bara hai. Ek unit circle (aisa circle jis ka radius 1 ho) lijiye jis ka centre origin \(O\) par ho. Angles \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) ki terminal sides (angle ki ghoomne wali aakhri lakeer) circle ko \(A\) aur \(B\) par kaatti hain. Zaahir hai ke \(m\angle AOB = \alpha - \beta\), kyun ke bara angle \(\alpha\) hai aur us mein se chhota angle \(\beta\) nikal diya. Ab circle par ek aur point \(C\) aisa lijiye ke \(m\angle XOC = m\angle AOB = \alpha - \beta\), yani wahi angle ab \(x\)-axis se naapa gaya. Phir \(A, B\) ko aur \(C, D\) ko milaiye.

blocks.alt: Unit circle with centre O on the axes X prime X and Y. Terminal sides of angles alpha and beta meet the circle at A(cos alpha, sin alpha) and B(cos beta, sin beta). Point C(cos(alpha minus beta), sin(alpha minus beta)) is on the circle so that angle XOC equals angle AOB equals alpha minus beta; D is (1, 0). Chords AB and CD are drawn.
blocks.caption: Figure: unit circle for the proof of the fundamental law (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Unit circle ka kamaal yeh hai: agar kisi angle \(\theta\) ki terminal side unit circle ko point \((x, y)\) par kaate, to \(\cos\theta = \frac{x}{1} = x\) aur \(\sin\theta = \frac{y}{1} = y\). Matlab unit circle ka har point \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) ki shakal mein likha ja sakta hai. Point \(D\) woh jagah hai jahan circle positive \(x\)-axis ko milta hai, yani angle \(0\) ki terminal side: \((\cos 0, \sin 0) = (1, 0)\).

Ab angles \(\alpha\), \(\beta\) aur \(\alpha - \beta\) standard position mein hain (vertex origin par, pehli side positive \(x\)-axis par). Is liye upar wale qaide se:
\(A\) ke coordinates \((\cos\alpha, \sin\alpha)\) hain,
\(B\) ke coordinates \((\cos\beta, \sin\beta)\) hain,
\(C\) ke coordinates \((\cos(\alpha - \beta), \sin(\alpha - \beta))\) hain,
aur \(D\) ke coordinates \((1, 0)\) hain.

Ab \(\triangle AOB\) aur \(\triangle COD\) congruent (bilkul ek jaise) hain [(SAS) theorem]. Is liye
\[|\overline{AB}| = |\overline{CD}|\]
\[\Rightarrow |\overline{AB}|^{2} = |\overline{CD}|^{2}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Triangles congruent kyun hain? \(OA = OC = 1\) aur \(OB = OD = 1\), kyun ke yeh sab unit circle ke radius hain. Aur in ke darmiyan wale angles barabar hain: \(m\angle AOB = m\angle COD = \alpha - \beta\). Do sides aur un ke beech ka angle barabar hon to triangles congruent hote hain: yahi SAS (Side-Angle-Side) rule hai. Congruent triangles ki teesri side bhi barabar hoti hai, is liye chord AB = chord CD.
Dono taraf square kyun kiya? Taa ke distance formula ka square root hat jaye aur hisaab saaf ho jaye.

Ab distance formula lagate hain. Left side par A aur B ke coordinates, right side par C aur D ke coordinates:
\[(\cos\alpha - \cos\beta)^{2} + (\sin\alpha - \sin\beta)^{2}\]
\[= [\cos(\alpha-\beta) - 1]^{2} + [\sin(\alpha-\beta) - 0]^{2}\]
Dono taraf squares kholne se:
\[\Rightarrow \cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta - 2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\]
\[\quad + \sin^{2}\alpha + \sin^{2}\beta - 2\sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[= \cos^{2}(\alpha-\beta) + 1 - 2\cos(\alpha-\beta)\]
\[\quad + \sin^{2}(\alpha-\beta)\]
\[\Rightarrow 2 - 2(\cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta)\]
\[= 2 - 2\cos(\alpha - \beta)\]
Lihaza
\[\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Doosre \(\Rightarrow\) wala qadam kaise aaya? Yahan \(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\) teen dafa laga hai: \(\cos^{2}\alpha + \sin^{2}\alpha = 1\), \(\cos^{2}\beta + \sin^{2}\beta = 1\), aur \(\cos^{2}(\alpha-\beta) + \sin^{2}(\alpha-\beta) = 1\). Left side par do jori, yani \(1 + 1 = 2\); right side par ek jori aur ek akela 1, yani phir 2. Is liye dono taraf \(2 - 2(\dots)\) bachta hai.\nAakhri qadam: dono taraf se 2 hata dein, phir \(-2\) se divide kar dein. Bas law haazir! Ghor kariye, yeh bilkul Example 1(ii) wala tareeqa hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Agarche yeh law humne \(\alpha > \beta > 0\) ke liye saabit kiya hai, lekin yeh \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) ki har value ke liye sach hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(\alpha = \beta\) rakh kar dekhiye: left side \(\cos 0 = 1\), right side \(\cos^{2}\alpha + \sin^{2}\alpha = 1\). Dono barabar! Is tarah aap formula ko kisi bhi aasan value se khud parakh sakte hain.
Ab kitab kehti hai: agar humein do angles \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) ke sin aur cos maloom hon, to is law se \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\) nikaal sakte hain, jaisa agli misaal mein samjhaya gaya hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Ek baat pehle se bata doon: Example 2 mein sin poocha gaya hai, aur kitab us ke hal mein \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\) istemal karti hai, jo asal mein agle page (10.1.2, result (v)) par saabit hota hai. Hum kitab ka tareeqa follow karenge, aur Tasdeeq wale qadam mein yahi jawab seedha fundamental law se nikaal kar dikhayenge, taa ke aap ko yaqeen ho jaye.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps:
Given: angle \(\frac{5\pi}{12}\) (radians mein).
To find: \(\sin\frac{5\pi}{12}\) ki exact (bilkul theek) value, tables ya calculator ke baghair.
Method: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke \(\frac{5\pi}{12}\) koi standard angle nahin, is ki value humein zabani yaad nahin. Lekin agar ise do aise angles ke jama mein tor dein jin ke sin aur cos humein yaad hain, jaise \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{6}\), to sum formula se kaam ban jayega.

Step 1: Angle ko standard angles ke jama mein likhein
\[\frac{5\pi}{12} = \frac{5 \times 180^{\circ}}{12} = 75^{\circ}\]
\[75^{\circ} = 45^{\circ} + 30^{\circ} = \frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\pi}{6}\]
Kyun: \(\pi\) radian \(= 180^{\circ}\), is liye \(\frac{5\pi}{12}\) ko degrees mein badalne se \(75^{\circ}\) mila. \(75^{\circ}\) hamari standard values ki list mein nahin, lekin \(45^{\circ}\) aur \(30^{\circ}\) hain, aur in ka jama theek \(75^{\circ}\) hai.

Step 2: Sum formula lagayein
\[\sin\frac{5\pi}{12} = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\]
\[= \sin\frac{\pi}{4}\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + \cos\frac{\pi}{4}\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\]
Kyun: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\), jahan \(\alpha = \frac{\pi}{4}\) aur \(\beta = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Yaad rakhiye: sin wale formula mein ratios mix hote hain (sin cos, cos sin), aur jama ke liye plus.

Step 3: Standard values rakhein
\[\sin\frac{\pi}{4} = \cos\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\ \sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\]
\[\sin\frac{5\pi}{12} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: yeh \(45^{\circ}\) aur \(30^{\circ}\) ki jaani pehchaani values hain. \(45^{\circ}\) par sin aur cos dono \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) hote hain; \(30^{\circ}\) par sin \(\frac{1}{2}\) aur cos \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

Step 4: Fractions jama karein
\[= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{2}} + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: dono fractions ka denominator same hai, \(2\sqrt{2}\), is liye sirf numerators jama karte hain. Agar upar neeche \(\sqrt{2}\) se multiply karein to rationalised (denominator se root hata hua) shakal \(\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}\) milti hai; dono jawab sahi hain.

Tasdeeq: yahi value fundamental law se
\[\sin 75^{\circ} = \cos 15^{\circ} = \cos(45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ})\]
\[= \cos 45^{\circ}\cos 30^{\circ} + \sin 45^{\circ}\sin 30^{\circ}\]
\[= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}\]
Bilkul wahi jawab! Yahan \(\sin 75^{\circ} = \cos 15^{\circ}\) is liye likha ke \(\sin\theta = \cos(90^{\circ} - \theta)\) hota hai (10.1.2 ka result (i)). Calculator se bhi dekh lein: \(\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.9659\), aur \(\sin 75^{\circ} \approx 0.9659\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: \(\cos 15^{\circ}\) seedha fundamental law se nikaaliye.
\(15^{\circ} = 60^{\circ} - 45^{\circ}\), is liye \(\cos 15^{\circ} = \cos 60^{\circ}\cos 45^{\circ} + \sin 60^{\circ}\sin 45^{\circ}\).
\(= \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{2}}\).
Dekha? \(45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ}\) lein ya \(60^{\circ} - 45^{\circ}\), jawab ek hi aata hai. Aur yeh wahi value hai jo \(\sin 75^{\circ}\) ki thi, kyun ke \(15^{\circ}\) aur \(75^{\circ}\) complementary (jama \(90^{\circ}\)) hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Fundamental law: \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\), har \(\alpha, \beta\) ke liye sach.
2. Bracket mein minus, right side par plus.
3. Saboot ka khulasa: unit circle par chord \(AB\) = chord \(CD\) (SAS se); distance formula se dono ke squares likhein; \(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta = 1\) se simplify karein.
4. Unit circle par angle \(\theta\) ki terminal side wala point \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) hota hai.
5. Ghair-standard angle ko standard angles ke jama ya farq mein toriye: \(75^{\circ} = 45^{\circ} + 30^{\circ}\), \(15^{\circ} = 45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ}\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha - \cos\beta\) likh dena. Yeh bilkul ghalat hai. Aazmaa kar dekhiye: \(\cos(90^{\circ} - 30^{\circ}) = \cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\), jab ke \(\cos 90^{\circ} - \cos 30^{\circ} = 0 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).
2. Law mein beech ka sign minus likh dena. \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\) mein beech ka sign plus hai.
3. Ratios ki ghalat jori: is law mein \(\cos\alpha\cos\beta\) aur \(\sin\alpha\sin\beta\) aate hain, \(\sin\alpha\cos\beta\) nahin. Mixed jori sin wale formulas mein aati hai.
4. Radians ko degrees mein badalte waqt \(\pi = 180^{\circ}\) bhool jana.
